nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 24 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 24 mmol Na2MoO4·2H2O were dissolved into 360 mL deionized water and formed a transparent green solution. The solution was then transferred into a 500-mL Teflon-lined autoclave, and four pieces of nickel foam were added. After reaction at 120°C for 6 h, the nickel foam samples were taken out, washed, and vacuum dried, and NiMoO4·×H2O arrays were obtained.

nodes.name: Anodic reconstruction to CR-NiOOH
nodes.procedure: First, NiMoO4·×H2O nanowire/nanosheet arrays on nickel foam were fabricated following previous reports. Next, the anodic oxidation process on Ni-MoO4·×H2O precursor was carried out in the standard three-electrode system in 1 M KOH and operated on an CHI760E electrochemical analyzer. A piece of Ni-MoO4·×H2O served as a working electrode, and the graphite rod and the unused Hg/HgO electrode served as a counterelectrode and a reference electrode, respectively. After carrying out CV tests in 0.924-1.724 V_RHE at a scan rate of 50 mV s^-1 for 30 cycles, black CR-NiOOH nanowire/nanosheet arrays were obtained with a mass loading of ~1.2 mg cm^-2.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiMoO4·xH2O nanowires are monocrystalline with smooth surface as revealed by TEM imaging.
nodes.evidence_snippet: These nanowires are monocrystalline with a smooth surface, confirmed by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) imaging and the corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Figure S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern confirms monocrystalline nature of NiMoO4·xH2O nanowires.
nodes.evidence_snippet: These nanowires are monocrystalline with a smooth surface, confirmed by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) imaging and the corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Figure S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD pattern of NiMoO4·xH2O is similar to CoMoO4·0.75H2O; crystal structure determined via atomic substitution and optimization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Its crystal structure was determined via atomic substitution and structure optimization because the powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern is similar to that of the reported analog CoMoO4·0.75H2O.

nodes.characterization_summary: CR-NiOOH nanowire interconnected by sub-5-nm ultrasmall nanoparticles with ~5-nm nanopores.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM imaging clearly demonstrates its morphological characterization... Such a nanowire is interconnected by sub-5-nm ultrasmall nanoparticles (NPs), resulting in visible interspaces with ~5-nm nanopores...

nodes.characterization_summary: CR-NiOOH NPs indexed to orthorhombic NiOOH planes: 0.158 nm (220), 0.208 nm (210), 0.213 nm (111), 0.240 nm (011), 0.248 nm (101).
nodes.evidence_snippet: All interplanar spacings of NPs within the nanowire are well indexed to the planes of NiOOH... The exposed interplanar spacings of 0.158, 0.208, 0.213, 0.240, and 0.248 nm can be well assigned to the (220), (210), (111), (011), and (101) planes...

nodes.characterization_summary: CR-NiOOH shows O/Ni atomic ratio of 2.05 and negligible Mo content (0.1 at.%).
nodes.evidence_snippet: ...the O/Ni atomic ratio is 2.05 from the corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy spectrum... negligible content (0.1 atomic percentage [at.%]) of the Mo element...

nodes.characterization_summary: CR-NiOOH shows only two Raman peaks at 474 cm⁻¹ (e_g bending) and 554 cm⁻¹ (A1g stretching vibration) of Ni-O, confirming pure NiOOH phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Only two Raman peaks at 474 and 554 cm⁻¹ belonging to the e_g bending and the A1g stretching vibration of Ni-O in NiOOH are observed (Figure S4E)...

nodes.characterization_summary: NiMoO4@NiOOH shows core-shell structure with 7-nm-thick NiOOH layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Only an 7-nm-thick NiOOH layer forms, and the inner continuous lattice fringes covering dozens of nanometers are indexed to the planes of NiMoO4...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman at 0.924-1.824 V_RHE in 1 M KOH shows NiMoO4·xH2O gradually reconstructs to CR-NiOOH (NiOOH peaks at 474, 554 cm⁻¹ appear at 1.424 V_RHE) while NiMoO4 remains almost unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Potential-dependent in situ Raman spectra of (A) NiMoO4$xH2O$ and (B) NiMoO4 at 0.924-1.824 V_RHE with the interval voltage of 50 mV in 1 M KOH, showing that NiMoO4$xH2O$ gradually reconstructs to CR-NiOOH but NiMoO4 is almost unchanged.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ XRD shows disappearance of NiMoO4·xH2O peaks at ~27.3° and 29.8°, indicating structural crack and amorphization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With the ex situ XRD measurement, disappearance of the representative peaks at ~27.3° and 29.8°, which belong to NiMoO4$xH2O$, demonstrates its structural crack and amorphization.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ XRD after alkali soaking shows Ni(OH)2 and K2MoO4 phases from etching reaction: NiMoO4·xH2O + 2OH⁻ → Ni(OH)2 + xH2O + MoO4²⁻.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ex situ XRD patterns of NiMoO4$xH2O$ after soaking in 1 M KOH. The detected K2MoO4 and Ni(OH)2 suggest the etching reaction (NiMoO4·xH2O + 2OH⁻ → Ni(OH)2 + xH2O + MoO4²⁻).
